body:
Partners Group is asking its shareholders to sign off on a structural overhaul of its largest open-ended vehicle, even as senior figures at the Swiss asset manager dig into their own pockets to signal conviction in the firm's prospects.

The Zug-based group has proposed splitting its flagship Global Value SICAV, which carries a net asset value of EUR 6.6 billion, into two standalone sub-funds. Subject to investor approval, one sleeve would chase long-term capital appreciation while the other would be geared toward distributing income generated by the portfolio. The move is designed to give clients a clearer choice between accumulation and payout profiles.

That proposal lands alongside a fresh product launch. Roughly a week ago, Partners Group rolled out a global private credit income strategy, structured as an open-ended evergreen fund and aimed at wealthy individuals and institutional investors hunting for yield in direct lending.

Behind the product changes sits a quieter reorganization of the firm's traditional private equity operation. Bloomberg reported that Partners Group has cut dozens of positions in the buyout unit or shifted staff into other parts of the business, with some employees leaving the company altogether and others moving into areas such as infrastructure and royalties.

Management pushed back on any suggestion of a broad retreat. A company spokesperson said team headcount remains in line with its long-run average and pointed to strengthened operational leadership capacity. Even so, the adjustments underscore how established buyout houses are recalibrating their structures as dealmaking and exit conditions become tougher to navigate.

Listed Vehicle Heads for Wind-Down

Investor preferences are reshaping the listed side of the business too. At Partners Group Private Equity Limited in London, shareholders voted roughly a week ago to pursue a liquidation option, with 74.1 percent of shares cast in favor. A previously planned restructuring of the listed vehicle was shelved as a result, and the portfolio will now be realized through an orderly wind-down.

Insiders Open Their Wallets

Confidence-building has come from the top. Between October 6 and 8, members of the management team plowed around CHF 21 million into the company's own shares. Combined with earlier purchases, private stock acquisitions by the leadership group have reached nearly CHF 39 million since the start of September.

Market watchers typically read such insider buying as an attempt to steady nerves during choppy trading, tying executives' personal wealth to the share price's future path.

The stock has been finding firmer ground of late. It closed yesterday at EUR 648.40, a gain of 1.4 percent on the day, and was trading friendlier at EUR 657.40 in today's session. The broader trend, however, remains punishing: the shares are down 38 percent year-to-date, a figure the other side of the reporting puts at 39 percent.

Investors looking for hard numbers on the firm's fundamental trajectory will have to wait until early next year. Partners Group has scheduled the release of its assets under management figures as of December 31 for January 13, 2027, after the market closes.
